excerpt: Denmark is navigating a delicate moment, balancing a slowing but still-expanding economy against a rapid acceleration in defense and internal security spending. Quarterly growth has cooled sharply, even as the government raised its full-year outlook, while new anti-drone systems and expanded conscription signal a decisive shift in national priorities. The tension between welfare continuity and a hardening security posture is reshaping Danish politics and carries lessons for the broader European Union.

title: Sweden's Recovery Looks Better on Paper Than in People's Wallets
excerpt: Sweden's economy grew 1.6 percent in the second quarter of 2026, prompting the government to upgrade its full-year growth forecast to 2.5 percent. But official statistics are doing little to lift the mood of households still grappling with high unemployment and financial strain. With a general election approaching and polls favouring the opposition, the gap between macroeconomic data and lived experience has become the defining political battleground.
